personality_traits: self-aware and wry - narrates her own domestic frustration straight to camera rather than confronting her partner
patient on the surface but visibly counting/keeping score ("I've said six things")
multitasker - keeps knitting steadily through the whole exchange, treating the recurring standoff as routine rather than a crisis
dryly resigned rather than angry - lands the complaint as a deadpan joke, not a fight
emotional_range: mild, patient neutrality while offering dinner options
faint knowing smirk as she reels off the rejected options
peak exasperation with mouth open on "I've said six things and he said no to all of them"
dry, almost fond resignation on "He has preferences" / "He just wants me to guess them"
expressions: 0:00 neutral, slightly heavy-lidded eyes while asking "What do you want to have for dinner?"
0:03 half-smile/raised brow on "Pizza?" as if already expecting a no
0:04 mouth flattens, eyes narrow slightly on "Not pizza"
0:05-0:07 eyebrows up, mouth open in an exasperated near-laugh delivering "I've said six things and he said no to all of them", eyes cut toward camera
0:08 lids droop back down, small wry mouth curl on "He has preferences"
0:10 faint closed-mouth smile, eyes rolled slightly on the punchline "He just wants me to guess them"
gestures: continuous, unbroken knitting motion (yarn ball and needles in hand) through nearly every line, hands never stop even as her face escalates
slight forward lean and direct look into camera when delivering the punchline lines, breaking the fourth wall
no touching or reaching toward the man beside her - stays self-contained in her own seat
characters.interactions_notes: She sits center-frame on the main sofa and speaks past the man rather than to him, addressing the audience directly for the recap/punchline lines - a classic complaint-to-camera setup. She never turns to face him or waits for a reply; the joke is that she is having (and narrating) an entire exasperating exchange essentially by herself.

personality_traits: checked-out / low-energy - the visual embodiment of the series title 'Low Battery People'
fussy, repetitive tic-driven behavior (constantly adjusting his glasses) that reads as nervous habit or total disengagement rather than active listening
non-verbal in this scene - his 'preferences' are only ever reported by her, he is never shown speaking or reacting
emotional_range: blank, deadpan throughout - no visible shift in emotion across the entire sequence
expressions: 0:00-0:10 unchanging heavy-lidded, half-closed eyes and a flat downturned mouth in every frame he appears in
no eye contact with the woman and no reaction to her escalating exasperation at any point
gestures: repeatedly lifts both hands to push his round glasses up and pull them back down / off his face, a looping fidget that recurs across nearly every frame
otherwise sits rigidly upright, arms mostly returning to the same position, facing forward rather than toward her
characters.interactions_notes: Positioned just to her left in his own chair, angled slightly away; he is present in frame for the entire scene but functions as an inert prop - the punchline depends on his total obliviousness while she vents about him. There is no dialogue, eye contact, or gesture exchanged between the two characters; the power dynamic is entirely one-directional, with her actively narrating and him passively, silently existing.
